ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the sector $AOB$, $\angle AOB=90^\circ$, with radius $OA=6$. When the sector $AOB$ is folded along the line passing through point $B$, point $O$ falls exactly on point $D$ on the arc $AB$. What is the area of the entire shaded region? (Express in terms of $\pi$)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $OD$. According to the properties of folding, $CD=CO$, $BD=BO$, $\angle DBC=\angle OBC$,\\
$\therefore OB=OD=BD$, i.e., $\triangle OBD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle DBO=60^\circ$, $\therefore \angle CBO= \frac{1}{2} \angle DBO=30^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle AOB=90^\circ$, $\therefore OC=OB \cdot \tan \angle CBO=6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} =2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle BDC}=S_{\triangle OBC}= \frac{1}{2} \times OB \times OC= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 2\sqrt{3} =6\sqrt{3}$,\\
$S_{\text{sector} AOB}= \frac{90}{360} \pi \times 6^2=9\pi$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the entire shaded region is: $S_{\text{sector} AOB}-S_{\triangle BDC}-S_{\triangle OBC}=9\pi-6\sqrt{3}-6\sqrt{3} =9\pi-12\sqrt{3}$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $9\pi-12\sqrt{3}=\boxed{9\pi-12\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 90° sector AOB with O as the center of the circle; OA is in the vertical direction on the left side, OB is in the horizontal direction at the bottom, and arc AB goes from A through D to B. Point C is on OA, and the crease is the line segment BC passing through B and C; after folding, point O falls on point D on arc AB. The shaded part in the figure consists of two pieces: one near A, C, D and arc AD, and the other near D, B and arc DB; the middle triangles OBC and BDC are unshaded. Reasoning: It is known that OA=OB=6, and ∠AOB=90°. When folding, O is mapped to D with respect to the crease BC, so B remains fixed on the crease, hence BO=BD; at the same time, D is on arc AB with O as the center of the circle, so OD=6. Also OB=6, therefore OB=OD=BD=6, triangle OBD is an equilateral triangle, and ∠OBD=60°. The crease BC is the axis of reflection, so it bisects ∠OBD, giving ∠OBC=30°. In right triangle OBC, OC is perpendicular to OB, and OB=6, therefore OC=OB·tan30°=6·√3/3=2√3. Thus S_{△OBC}=1/2·OB·OC=1/2·6·2√3=6√3. By folding symmetry, S_{△BDC}=S_{△OBC}=6√3. The area of sector AOB is (90/360)π·6²=9π. The entire shaded area equals the sector area minus the areas of the two unshaded triangles, so it is 9π-6√3-6√3=9π-12√3.
